subject: combined-science

items.q: A structure in an organism is made up of several different tissues that work together to carry out a specific function. Which level of organisation is this structure?
items.correct: an organ, an aggregation of tissues
items.misconception: a tissue, a group of similar cells
items.why: Students remember the short phrase 'a tissue is a group of cells' and drop the rest of the definition. Diagrams of body structures show many kinds of cell side by side, so students label the whole group as one tissue and skip the organ level. A tissue is a group of cells with a similar structure and function. Cells are the basic building blocks of all living organisms; where several different tissues are grouped together the structure is an organ, because organs are aggregations of tissues performing specific functions.
items.random_wrong: an organ system, a group of several organs

items.q: Which statement about organ systems in a living organism is correct?
items.correct: Organ systems are made of organs that work together.
items.misconception: Organ systems are made of one organ with one function.
items.why: The name of a system sounds like the name of one structure, so students picture a system as a single object rather than as several organs. The organism level is then treated as the next step up from a single organ. Organs are organised into organ systems, which work together to form organisms, so an organ system is a group of organs rather than one organ.
items.random_wrong: Organ systems are made of cells grouped together.

items.q: How many tissues make up an organ?
items.correct: An organ is an aggregation of tissues, so one organ is normally made from more than one tissue working together to perform a specific function.
items.misconception: An organ is made from only one type of tissue, so an organ and a tissue are really the same level of organisation.
items.why: Both tissues and organs are described as carrying out a function, so students treat the two words as interchangeable. Naming a single tissue inside a named organ reinforces the idea that one organ equals one tissue. A tissue is a group of cells with a similar structure and function, whereas organs are aggregations of tissues performing specific functions, so several different tissues can make up one organ.
items.note: no MCQ covers this misconception, so no third distractor was authored for it; none invented
